questions.q: An INAV profile has `roll_rate = 45`. What is the roll rate at full stick?
options: 45 % of the rate set in Betaflight
questions.explain: INAV rates are set in tens of °/s (`pidRcCommandToRate`: maxRate = rate · 10). The range of `roll_rate` is 4…180, that is, 40…1800 °/s.

questions.q: `mc_i_roll = 30`. What is the gain kI the controller works with?
options: 0.97 — the divisor is 31, as for P
30 — the number is used as is
questions.explain: `pid.h`: P is divided by 31, I by 4, D by 1905, CD by 7270. At an error of 10 °/s the integral grows by 75 units a second until I-term relax and the 33 % limit stop it.

questions.q: A fragment of the config of a quadcopter on INAV 9.1. What about the RPM filter?
questions.fragment:
serial 1 2 115200 115200 0 115200
serial 2 64 115200 115200 0 115200
set motor_pwm_protocol = DSHOT600
set motor_poles = 14
set rpm_gyro_filter_enabled = ON
set rpm_gyro_harmonics = 1
options: It works: RPM comes over the same DShot line
It is not initialized: there is no ESC telemetry port
It works only on the first harmonic of each motor
It works but is updated at 500 Hz instead of 2 kHz
questions.explain: INAV 9.1.0 has no bidirectional DShot. RPM is read from ESC telemetry over a UART with function 262144; in the config the port functions are 2 (GPS) and 64 (receiver). `fc_init.c` starts the RPM filter only with an ESC telemetry port open.

questions.q: EZ Tune is enabled, `ez_response = 120`, `ez_axis_ratio = 110`, the other sliders are at their defaults. What `mc_p_pitch` does the firmware write?
questions.explain: Roll P = 40 · 120 / 100 = 48; pitch P = 48 · 110 / 100 = 52.8, the fractional part is dropped — 52. 44 would be the result at response 100.

questions.q: Which INAV filter is the only one that runs at the gyro sampling rate rather than in the PID task?
questions.explain: `gyroUpdate()` applies only the anti-alias PT1 (250 Hz). The RPM notch, LULU, the main LPF, the dynamic notch and Kalman are in `gyroFilter()`, which the PID task calls with the period `looptime`.

questions.q: What does `mc_d_level = 75` mean on a multirotor?
options: The D term of the ANGLE loop, like `mc_d_roll` in the rate loop
The cutoff of the angle loop filter, 75 Hz
A stick travel of 75 %, above which HORIZON controls by rate
A maximum tilt angle of 75° in HORIZON mode
questions.explain: In the LEVEL block the only real controller is P (`mc_p_level` / 6.56). `mc_i_level` is the cutoff of the PT1 on the rate setpoint in hertz, `mc_d_level` is the HORIZON transition point in percent of stick travel.

questions.q: POSHOLD. The aircraft was flying at 8 m/s, after the stick was released it stopped after 13 m and came back. What do you change first?
questions.fragment:
set nav_mc_pos_deceleration_time = 120
set nav_mc_pos_xy_p = 65
set nav_mc_vel_xy_dterm_attenuation = 90
set nav_mc_bank_angle = 35
questions.explain: The stop target is placed 8 · 1.2 = 9.6 m ahead, and the aircraft needs 13 m: it passes the target and comes back. 13 / 8 = 1.63 s, so the value is no less than 163. A larger position P makes the return sharper, a smaller angle makes the braking distance longer, and the attenuation of D at speed has nothing to do with the stop point.

questions.q: `nav_mc_bank_angle = 35`, `max_angle_inclination_rll = 250`, `max_angle_inclination_pit = 250`. What is the largest angle navigation will command?
questions.explain: The navigation angle is passed to the ANGLE loop through `pidAngleToRcCommand`, which clips it by `max_angle_inclination_*` (decidegrees: 250 = 25°). The smaller of the two limits applies, and the acceleration is no more than g · tan 25° = 4.57 m/s².

questions.q: In POSHOLD the aircraft circles around the point, and the radius grows; in ANGLE it flies normally. The most likely cause?
questions.explain: The correction is computed in north–east axes and rotated into the aircraft axes by the current heading. A heading error turns it past the point — the result is a spiral. In the air you go to ANGLE at once; on the ground you check the alignment, calibration and interference of the compass.

questions.q: Which pair of settings does switching `control_profile` NOT change?
questions.explain: The gyro filters are common to all profiles, and `nav_mc_hover_thr` is in the battery profile. The PIDs, the navigation PIDs, `dterm_lpf_hz`, the rates, TPA and the EZ Tune sliders are part of the control profile.
